title: Eunuchs
lead: A eunuch was a castrated man; kings across the ancient Near East used eunuchs as trusted officials, so the Hebrew word saris also came to mean "court official." The Law kept such men out of Israel's assembly, the prophets promised them a place, and the New Testament shows a eunuch among the first to be baptized.

sections.b: Because they could found no family of their own, eunuchs were trusted in palaces as guards of the women's quarters, treasurers and advisers. The Hebrew saris covers both senses, and context decides: Potiphar, who had a wife, is a saris of Pharaoh, best taken as "court official" (Genesis 39:1). Eunuchs serve the kings of Israel and Judah (1 Kings 22:9; 2 Kings 9:32), Babylon (Daniel 1:3) and Persia, where seven eunuchs wait on Ahasuerus and Hegai keeps the women (Esther 1:10; 2:3). Ebed-melech, the Cushite official who rescued Jeremiah, is called a saris (Jeremiah 38:7).
sections.refs: Genesis 39:1; 1 Kings 22:9; 2 Kings 9:32; 2 Kings 20:18; Esther 1:10; Esther 2:3; Daniel 1:3; Jeremiah 38:7

sections.b: Deuteronomy shut men who had been castrated out of "the assembly of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 23:1), as it shut out some foreign peoples, for reasons the text does not give. Some think a body made unwhole could not stand for the wholeness of God's people (compare Leviticus 21:16–23 for priests); others think the rule rejected the cult castration of some pagan priests, such as the galli who served the goddess Cybele (compare Deuteronomy 14:1 against pagan mourning cuts). Isaiah 56:3–5 answers with one of the boldest promises of the prophets: eunuchs who keep the Sabbath and hold to the covenant will receive, in God's house, "a marker and a name / that is better than sons and daughters" (Isaiah 56:5). Jesus spoke of some who are eunuchs "because of the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 19:12; see the topic celibacy). In Acts 8 an Ethiopian eunuch, returning from worship in Jerusalem and reading Isaiah, asks what stops him from being baptized, and nothing does.
sections.refs: Deuteronomy 23:1; Leviticus 21:16–23; Isaiah 56:3–7; Wisdom 3:14; Matthew 19:12; Acts 8:26–39; Deuteronomy 14:1
